brief: Goldman Sachs FICC and Equities daily note dated 2 September 2026. Macro: August ISM manufacturing fell 1.0pt to 54.6, below expectations, with new orders, production and employment all lower, so cyclicals lagged defensives on the tape. Against that, the S&P Global manufacturing PMI was revised higher and Goldman's own manufacturing survey tracker hit its highest level since April 2022, so the desk reads regional surveys as improving despite the ISM print. July job openings rose 89k to 7,271k from a downwardly revised June, lifting the jobs-workers gap estimate to 0.3mn in August. Construction spending fell 0.5% in July. Q3 GDP tracking stays at +2.7%. Positioning: ETF shorts are 10.2% of the US equity short book excluding index products, down from 10.7% in July and in the 2nd percentile over one and five years. Equities closed lower Tuesday on rising yields and oil after the latest Iran escalation, SPX -71bps to 7631. DELL beat on F2Q27 EPS of $7.04 with ISG revenue +89% and raised its F2027 server and storage outlook, and shares indicated +8.4% after the bell.
